title: The Voynich Manuscript Code Has Finally Been Cracked...Or Not

  • Trillium Rare Prints
    Antique Prints, Maps, & Books of Natural History, Botanicals, & More
    November 28, 2026

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Curtis's Botanical Magazine - 20 Volumes bound in 10 with 786 Engravings. $8,000 to $12,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Munster, pub. 1542 - Map of the New World or the Americas. $10,000 to $15,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Catlin, Folio, On Card - North American Indians. $4,000 to $6,000.

    Trillium Rare Prints
    Antique Prints, Maps, & Books of Natural History, Botanicals, & More
    November 28, 2026

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Audubon, First Ed - Great Blue Heron. 369. $1,500 to $2,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Cassini - Map of Australia (New Holland). $4,000 to $6,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Temminck's Nouveau ..d'Oiseaux - Five Volumes with 600 Originally Hand-colored Engravings. $25,000 to $30,000.

    Trillium Rare Prints
    Antique Prints, Maps, & Books of Natural History, Botanicals, & More
    November 28, 2026

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Redoute, Choix - Tulip (var.) [Tulipa culta]. $1,000 to $2,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Sanson's Description de tout l’Univers... - Volume with 74 Hand-Colored Maps. $8,000 to $12,000.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Captain Cook, Hawaii - A Man of the Sandwich Islands, in a Mask [Homme masqué de l'isle Sandwich]. $500 to $1,000.

    Antique Prints, Maps, & Books of Natural History, Botanicals, & More
    November 28, 2026

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Catesby, First Ed - Osprey or Fishing Hawk. 1-2. $1,500 to $2,500.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Thornton – Tulips. $600 to $1,200.

    Trillium, Nov. 28: Karl Bodmer - Pehriska-Ruhpa, Moennitarri Warrior in the Costume of the Dog Danse. $6,000 to $12,000.

  • Arader Galleries
    Extraordinary Works of Art & World History
    December 5, 2026

    Arader, Dec. 5: Audubon Havell aquatint, Brown Pelican Standing, Plate 251 – State Bird of Louisiana. $100,000 to $150,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Bateman’s Orchids of Mexico and Guatelamal – The John Roland Abbey Example. $120,000 to $150,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: A beautifully detailed manuscript Book of Hours – Use of Rome, published in Barcelona c. 1490. $100,000 to $150,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Braun & Hogenburg – The first atlas of the cities of the world with splendid original Renaissance color. $400,000 to $600,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Brookshaw’s Pomona Britannica – “One of the finest colour-plate books in existence.” $70,000 to $100,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Mark Catesby’s 2nd edition of the Natural History of Carolina… “The most famous colorplate book of American plant and animal life.” $150,000 to $200,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Gould’s Birds of Europe – The beginning of the great project. $80,000 to $120,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Joinville’s History of Louis IX – Bound for Marie de’ Medici, Queen Regent of France. $35,000 to $55,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Moran’s The Yellowstone National Park, framed in 15 parts – The foundational document of the National Park Service. $250,000 to $350,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Ortelius’ Theatrum Orbis Terrarum – From the father of modern atlas-making – The Martelli Example. $175,000 to $250,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: The Foljambe Set of Pennant’s Zoology, with the maximum complement of plates. $50,000 to $70,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Ptolemy’s Geography 1511 edition, the first atlas with maps printed in red and black ink. $120,000 to $180,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Redoute Lillies wwith the plates bound alphabetically by genus in emulation of the rare large paper issue. $400,000 to $500,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Roberts’ Holy Land – “The finest illustrated travel book of the 19th century” – The apotheosis of the tinted lithograph. $90,000 to $120,000.

    Arader, Dec. 5: Vesalius’ De Humani Corporis – The renaissance of anatomy, the anatomy of the Renaissance. $350,000 to $450,000.

  • Sotheby’s
    Books & Manuscripts
    November & December Sales

    Sotheby’s, Dec. 2: Brian Jones | Charlie Watts. An extraordinary Rolling Stones founding document — The 1962 letter from Brian Jones to Charlie Watts, inviting him to join the band.

    Sotheby’s, Dec. 15: Illuminated manuscript, Sammelband of 9 works by Anselm of Canterbury with added sequence for Saint Ursula, (Germany, Cologne, Monastery of St Pantaleon), second half of the 12th century.

    Sotheby’s, Dec. 15: Illustrated manuscript, on vellum, in Latin, Raymond of Peñafort Summa de casibus and Summa de matrimonio, (Southern Germany or Alsace), second half of the 13th century (after 1234).

    Sotheby’s, Dec. 15: Manuscript, on vellum and paper, in German and Latin, The Johannes Libellum, Sammelband of 15 texts on the lives of Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist, last quarter of the 15th century (Southern Germany).

    Sotheby’s, Dec. 15: Rudimentum novitiorum, Lübeck, 1475, first edition, eighteenth-century armorial sheep, featuring the first modern printed map, a magnificent hand-coloured copy.

  • Heritage, Dec. 9: Philip K. Dick. Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? First edition, author Brian Aldiss’ copy.

    Heritage, Dec. 9: Robert A. Heinlein. Assignment in Eternity. First edition, inscribed by Heinlein to author “Doc” Smith.

    Heritage, Dec. 9: Frank Herbert. Dune. First edition, inscribed by Herbert to his literary agent.

    Heritage, Dec. 9: J. R. R. Tolkien. The Hobbit, or There and Back Again. First edition, first impression, in an unrestored dust jacket.

    Heritage, Dec. 9: Jules Verne. Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas. Exceedingly rare, perhaps unique variant, English sheets bound in an American Osgood binding.

    Heritage, Dec. 9: Isaac Asimov. The Naked Sun. First edition, inscribed by Asimov to Alex Berman, founder of Phantasia Press.
